_comment: FACTORtv — THE SEASON.
Every number in these lines is exact. They are filled from
season.Career.title_state(), which computes points available and
whether a leader can still be caught from recorded rounds only — so a
line saying 'he cannot be caught' is a claim the user can check against
his own standings table and find correct.
The gating in overlay_booth._season_call() matters as much as the
wording: no career, no line; fewer than TITLE_TALK_AFTER rounds in the
books, no title talk; an open season never gets 'of twenty-four' or any
title maths at all, because with no end date neither is true.
Slots: {n} round number, {total} rounds in the season, {event} the
round's proper name, {leader} championship leader, {pts} points,
{gap} points to the lead, {pos} his place in the table, {left} rounds
remaining.
`season_round_anytrack` is for a season with a declared
LENGTH but no fixed calendar — N races, anywhere. Those
rounds have no event name, so these lines name the
circuit instead and never reference {event}.
`season_midway` / `season_late` are the SEASON's own phases, from
season.Career.phase(). A season has a shape exactly as a race does, and
without saying so every round sounds identical except for its number.
`season_here` is track memory scoped to THIS season — a stronger thing to
say than a record from a career ago, and the only kind an open season can
have, since it may revisit a circuit.
`season_launch` is the FIRST session of a career and exists so the user
can hear that career mode is actually running — the format, the number of
rounds, and that there is a title at the end of it. {series} comes from
era.py's reading of the car class, so it names the championship without
the career having to be told what it is.
